subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Safety Systems: Protecting Humans from Robots
description: A 60-second lesson on Safety Systems: Protecting Humans from Robots.

hook.text: An industrial robot arm can exert 1,000 newtons of force. Without safety systems, it's a lethal hazard.

buildup.text: Light curtains detect when a person crosses into the danger zone. The robot stops instantly.

discovery.text: Safety-rated controllers monitor speed, position, and force. If any value exceeds limits, power is cut in milliseconds.

twist.text: Redundant safety circuits use two independent channels. Both must agree before the robot can move. One failure stops everything.

climax.text: ISO 10218 sets global robot safety standards. Every industrial robot installation must comply or face shutdown.

punchline.text: Robots are powerful. Safety systems make them livable.

quiz.question: Why do robot safety systems use dual-channel redundancy?
options: To double the processing speed of the safety controller
Both channels must agree before the robot moves — one failure stops everything
To allow the robot to operate at higher speeds safely
